conditions.browser: Chromium (Playwright build), macOS system fonts, deviceScaleFactor 1

candidates.name: s1C
candidates.idea: Test a middle width for Notes between s0B and T, seeking to keep date-fns together while reducing horizontal scrolling.
candidates.label: gold

lineInfo.text: Consider replacing with native methods to
In maintenance mode; migrate to date-fns
Pre-release build pinned by the platform

whys: The full table has even two-line content rows, a shorter package wrap and an intact version. At first sight, however, much of every note lies beyond the viewport, requiring substantial horizontal scrolling.

The package name and notes wrap into at most two lines, and the full prerelease version remains together. However, much of every note lies beyond the initial viewport, so reading notes requires substantial scrolling.

The long package and advisory URL each wrap over two lines, and the rows have a calm, consistent rhythm. The initial viewport cuts off much of Notes, so reading those details requires substantial scrolling.

candidates.name: d3r2A
candidates.idea: Test a viewport-fitting balance that keeps the prerelease version intact while giving notes 20px more than d3r1A. The package column still accommodates its longest unbreakable segment, though the full identifier will wrap.
candidates.label: gold

whys: The version stays on one line and the table fits. The long package wraps at hyphens and the advisory note occupies four lines, making that row relatively tall.

The full prerelease version stays together and all columns fit on screen. The long package name still takes three lines, and the constrained notes column produces several tall rows, including a four-line advisory.

The full table is visible and the prerelease version stays together, helping version lookup. The long package spans three lines and the narrow notes make several rows tall, especially the advisory row.

candidates.name: d1r1A
candidates.idea: Fitting alternative: reduce Version to its measured one-line requirement and give the recovered space to Notes. This retains all fields in the viewport and may improve prose wrapping, though the advisory still has to break.
candidates.label: gold

whys: It fits and gives notes slightly more room than B, but the prerelease version breaks across lines. The advisory note still takes four lines.
All columns are visible at once, and the package and advisory URL wrap at natural boundaries. The prerelease version splits, while the narrow notes column makes the advisory row four lines tall.
All columns are visible at once, but the long package spans three lines, the prerelease version wraps, and the advisory note takes four lines. The taller rows interrupt scanning.
The version remains intact and notes are shorter than in the fitting layouts. The initial viewport cuts off the ends of several notes, but the required scroll is modest.

The full version remains on one line, notes have reasonable line lengths, and the long package name wraps at hyphens. Some note endings are outside the initial viewport, requiring a small horizontal scroll.
The version stays whole and the notes read more comfortably than in the fitting layouts. The long package still takes three lines, and the first viewport cuts off the ends of several notes.

candidates.name: contrast
candidates.idea: Equal widths give excess space to short fields while forcing the package identifier and notes into narrow columns. The long package name and advisory URL would be fragmented, making lookup and continuous reading harder.
candidates.label: bad

whys: All content is present, but equal columns leave notes and the long package identifier cramped. Words and the advisory URL break internally, while short-value columns contain large areas of empty space.
Equal widths leave excessive space in the short-value columns and squeeze package names and notes. The package identifier and URL break inside words, making them harder to read and verify.
Equal columns leave Notes and the long package too narrow while short fields have excess space. The package and URL break within words, producing tall, fragmented rows.
The narrow version column splits the prerelease version, and the advisory URL runs past the initial viewport edge. The small scroll distance buys shorter notes but still interrupts lookup.

The compact table keeps most notes readable and requires little scrolling. The long package name occupies three lines, the prerelease version splits, and the advisory URL reaches beyond the initial viewport.

Most content is visible initially and the notes have useful room, but the long package occupies three lines and the prerelease version wraps. A small scroll is still needed to see the entire right edge.

d1.purpose: Audit dependencies by connecting each package and version to its license, vulnerability status, and maintenance or remediation notes.
tasks: Find a package and read across its row to assess its status.
Compare licenses and vulnerability counts across packages.
Read notes for context, follow-up actions, and the advisory reference.
relations: Version identifies the audited release of the package in the same row.
License and vulnerability status are compact attributes of that release.
Notes explain context or action; the advisory URL relates to the moderate vulnerability in the node-fetch row.
roles: The header names five fields; each body row represents one dependency.
Package names act as visual row identifiers even though no row headers are declared.
Version, license, and vulnerabilities support scanning and comparison; notes carry explanatory prose.
keep_whole: Package name segments and version identifiers where space permits.
License names, vulnerability values, and the Vulnerabilities header.
The advisory URL where space permits, so it remains easy to recognize and use.
may_wrap: Long package names at available natural break points.
In the fitting layout, the long advisory URL and possibly a package segment must break because the viewport cannot accommodate every unbreakable unit.
same_scale: Version, license, and vulnerability columns should remain compact and sized to their distinct contents.
Package and notes columns deserve more space because they carry longer identifiers and prose; their widths need not match.
d1.h_vs_v: A viewport-fitting table keeps all fields visible together but increases row height and forces breaks in long strings. Scrolling can preserve identifiers or notes more comfortably, at the cost of hiding right-hand fields until the reader scrolls.

d2.purpose: Present a dependency audit that connects each package to its version, license, vulnerability status and maintenance notes.
tasks: Find a package and read across its row.
Check licenses and versions, then follow up on relevant notes or advisories.
relations: Each row describes one package; the notes qualify its audit status.
The advisory URL belongs to the package with one moderate vulnerability.
roles: Package names identify records and anchor horizontal reading.
Version, license and vulnerabilities are compact lookup and comparison fields.
Notes provide prose context and occasionally a long advisory URL.
keep_whole: Package identifiers, including the scoped internal package
may_wrap: Long identifiers and the advisory URL only when the available width makes splitting unavoidable
same_scale: Version, license and vulnerability columns are compact, though the vulnerability heading needs more width.
Package and Notes deserve more space because they contain the longest text.
d2.h_vs_v: A viewport-fitting table keeps every field visible together but must split some long units and grow vertically. Scrolling allows identifiers and the advisory URL more room, at the cost of hiding some fields initially.

d3.purpose: Audit dependencies by connecting each package and version to its license, vulnerability status and maintenance notes.
tasks: Find a package and confirm its version.
Scan and compare license and vulnerability status across packages.
Read notes for recommended actions and advisory details.
relations: Each row describes one package; its version, license, vulnerability status and notes belong together.
The advisory URL explains the moderate vulnerability in the node-fetch row.
roles: Package names act as row identifiers even though no row headers are declared.
Version, license and vulnerability status are compact audit fields; notes provide supporting context and actions.
keep_whole: Package identifiers, especially the scoped internal package name, when space permits.
Version strings, license names, vulnerability counts and severity labels.
The advisory URL and inline code identifier date-fns when space permits.
may_wrap: Notes prose can wrap at natural word boundaries.
In a viewport-fitting design, the long package identifier and advisory URL must break within their strings.
same_scale: Version, license and vulnerability columns should remain compact and large enough for their values and headers.
Package and notes need more space, but their relative widths can reflect whether identifier lookup or prose reading takes priority.
d3.h_vs_v: Keeping all identifiers intact requires horizontal scrolling. Fitting the viewport preserves the complete row context at first sight but increases row height and forces breaks inside the longest package name and URL.

analysis.strengths: The whole table is visible at once, all headers remain on one line, and the package names have a little more room than in Q. The core audit fields are easy to scan across each row.
analysis.faults: The prerelease version wraps at its hyphen, the long package name occupies three lines, and the advisory note occupies four. The tall node-fetch row makes the table feel uneven.
analysis.spatial_logic: P keeps the license and vulnerability columns at their apparent minimums, gives the package column 168px, and assigns the remaining space to notes. It gains a little package space by narrowing the version column.

analysis.strengths: The entire table fits in the viewport, the headers stay on one line, and every version, including the prerelease, stays together.
analysis.faults: The narrower notes column adds a line to the moment row compared with P, while the narrower package column produces less natural breaks in the long identifier. The advisory note still takes four lines, making this the tallest proposal.
analysis.spatial_logic: Q transfers space from package and notes to version. Keeping versions intact is useful for an audit, but the transfer has a noticeable height cost.

analysis.strengths: All versions stay intact, the first four fields are visible on initial view, and the wider notes column reduces most notes to two lines. Its 113px overflow is the smallest among the scrolling proposals.
analysis.faults: The long package identifier still takes three lines. The initial viewport cuts through notes, so their complete text requires scrolling; the advisory URL also wraps.
analysis.spatial_logic: R preserves P's compact package width and Q's full version width, then spends the extra width on notes. It prioritizes a modest scroll distance over minimizing the longest package row.

analysis.strengths: Most rows are single-line and the full view is compact and easy to scan. Notes have enough space to keep even the advisory URL on one line, and the long package name needs only two lines.
analysis.faults: The initial viewport shows only the beginning of notes, and the 364px overflow requires substantial horizontal travel to read them. Wide columns also spread related audit fields apart.
analysis.spatial_logic: S spends generously on both package and notes to favor single-line reading. Its compact height comes at the cost of the widest horizontal footprint.

analysis.strengths: The long package name takes two lines, versions stay whole, and the four multi-line rows have a consistent height. It is substantially narrower than S while retaining readable two-line notes.
analysis.faults: The initial viewport shows only the start of notes, and reading their ends requires 190px of scrolling. The advisory URL wraps, and the package identifier still breaks across lines.
analysis.spatial_logic: T balances extra width between package and notes. It accepts some wrapping in exchange for a shorter table than R and less scrolling than S.

rounds.insights: The main trade-off is between seeing every field at once and preserving identifiers and notes in fewer lines. A full version width matters because the prerelease is an audit identifier; extra package width can reduce the long name from three lines to two, while extra notes width reduces prose and URL wrapping. The reported absence of breaks inside words does not mean identifiers or URLs remain on one line. In the scrolling class, the first four columns remain visible initially, but wider package columns leave less of each note visible. Exact gains from new widths require a render.

analysis.strengths: Compact, even two-line rows; the package identifier and version are easier to scan than in the fitting layout. All headers stay on one line.
analysis.faults: The date-fns identifier wraps across lines, and the advisory URL also wraps. Much of Notes lies beyond the initial viewport.
analysis.spatial_logic: The package column receives enough width for a two-line long identifier, while the narrow Notes column saves scrolling at the cost of less natural breaks.

analysis.strengths: Requires less scrolling than the other scrolling layouts and gives Notes more visible space at first sight. The wider Notes column keeps date-fns together.
analysis.faults: The long package identifier takes three lines, making its row taller and harder to scan. The advisory URL still wraps, and the ends of Notes require scrolling.
analysis.spatial_logic: Width moves from Package to Notes, improving prose and initial visibility but weakening the primary lookup field.

analysis.strengths: All columns are visible together, preserving the relationship between each package, its audit status and its notes without scrolling. Headers remain on one line.
analysis.faults: The long package identifier takes three lines, the prerelease version wraps, and the advisory note takes four lines. These breaks make the table tall and interrupt lookup.
analysis.spatial_logic: The width limit compresses both the lookup fields and Notes; the resulting uneven row heights are the price of a complete first view.

analysis.strengths: The long package identifier occupies two lines, the prerelease version and date-fns stay together, and all rows remain at most two lines tall. The wider Notes column gives prose more natural breaks.
analysis.faults: It requires the most scrolling, and the first viewport exposes only the beginning of Notes. The advisory URL still wraps.
analysis.spatial_logic: Generous widths for Package and Notes support continuous reading and a regular row rhythm, while the audit columns remain compact.

rounds.insights: Package identity and audit fields need to remain easy to scan together; Notes benefits from additional width but is the column most naturally reached by scrolling. The fitting layout makes every column visible but forces consequential breaks in the package, version and advisory. Among scrolling layouts, T improves the note breaks over s0B without increasing row heights, while s0C trades a shorter scroll for a more fragmented package identifier.

analysis.strengths: All headers and audit fields are legible, and the wider Notes column keeps the platform-team note on one line. The first four columns are visible initially.
analysis.faults: The long package identifier occupies three lines and makes its row noticeably taller. Notes require horizontal scrolling to read in full, and the advisory URL wraps.
analysis.spatial_logic: Space favors Notes over Package, but the narrower package column produces an isolated tall row without making Notes fully visible in the viewport.

analysis.strengths: The long package identifier fits on two lines, all versions remain whole, and the four middle data rows share a consistent height. The full table is compact and no word is broken internally.
analysis.faults: Most of each note is beyond the initial viewport. The platform-team note wraps a short final word onto a second line, and the advisory URL wraps.
analysis.spatial_logic: The wider Package column improves identifier scanning, while the narrower Notes column keeps the total scroll distance slightly below T's. The even row heights make cross-column comparison easy.

analysis.strengths: The entire table is visible without scrolling, all headers stay on one line, and the key audit columns can be compared at a glance.
analysis.faults: The prerelease version wraps at its hyphen, the long package identifier takes three lines, and the advisory note takes four. The resulting uneven row heights interrupt scanning; the URL also wraps across lines.
analysis.spatial_logic: The fit prioritizes simultaneous visibility, but the constrained Package and Notes columns concentrate height in the most complex rows. The version column is just too narrow to preserve the full prerelease identifier.

analysis.strengths: The package identifier and all notes use at most two lines, versions stay whole, and the platform-team note fits on one line. Consistent row heights and intact headers support a clear audit scan.
analysis.faults: It has the greatest horizontal overflow, while the first viewport shows only the beginning of Notes. The advisory URL still wraps.
analysis.spatial_logic: Package and Notes both receive enough width for comfortable reading in the full table, at the cost of more scrolling. Its extra Notes width improves one cell without reducing overall table height.

rounds.insights: The main trade-off is between seeing every column at once and preserving compact, readable identifiers and notes. Increasing Package from 210 to 235 px removes a third line and regularizes the scrolling layouts. T's extra Notes width improves one note over s1C but increases scrolling without shortening the table. In the fitting layout, preserving the prerelease version deserves a small transfer of width even if Notes becomes slightly narrower.

bad.why: The narrow Version column splits the prerelease version across lines, making an important audit identifier harder to read and compare.
The very wide Notes column leaves most notes beyond the initial viewport and requires 364 px of scrolling, a large cost for keeping prose on one line.

contrast.why: Equal widths give excess space to short fields while forcing the package identifier and notes into narrow columns. The long package name and advisory URL would be fragmented, making lookup and continuous reading harder.

sameFunctionGroups.why: These are compact audit attributes, but their headers and values have different width needs. Each should be wide enough for its own content rather than forced to match its neighbors.

synthesis.rationale: s1C keeps versions and compact audit fields intact, gives the long package identifier two lines, and maintains a regular row rhythm. Q is the stronger fitting choice because its version remains whole, though the package name and advisory reference wrap and the notes make several rows tall. T is also publishable, but its extra width over s1C buys only a modest improvement in one note.

general: Protect identifiers and comparison fields from avoidable breaks before optimizing table height.
Judge scrolling layouts in both the full table and the initial viewport.
Allocate widths according to content and reading tasks rather than equalizing columns by default.
specific: Allow enough width for the prerelease version to remain on one line.
A two-line package identifier and notes provide a useful balance between row height and horizontal scrolling.

synthesis.tradeoffs: Q exposes every column at once but produces taller rows and more fragmented notes. s1C is more compact and easier to scan, but readers must scroll to finish the notes; narrower scrolling options reduce that distance at the cost of a three-line package identifier.
synthesis.uncertain: The best choice depends on how often readers need full notes alongside package names and how discoverable horizontal scrolling is in the actual interface.

critique.good: All five fields are visible together, and the compact status columns support comparison. Headers, versions, licenses, and vulnerability values remain readable.
critique.problems: The notes are dense and create tall rows; the advisory URL breaks inside a word, making it harder to recognize. The long package name occupies three lines.
critique.cause: The 217 px Notes column is too narrow for the advisory URL and comfortable prose. The 168 px Package column fits its longest unbreakable segment but leaves the full identifier heavily wrapped.

critique.good: The long package name stays on one line, and all content is accessible in the full table without measured breaks inside words.
critique.problems: The package column leaves extensive empty space in most rows. At first sight the vulnerability column is cut off and Notes is entirely beyond the viewport, separating key audit fields from their context. Notes still wrap into two or three lines.
critique.cause: The 412 px Package column is sized for one exceptional identifier, pushing the status and notes columns to the right. The 273 px Notes column is much narrower than the package column despite carrying longer prose.

critique.good: The compact package column keeps all status fields and the start of Notes visible initially. In the full table, notes read comfortably on single lines and the advisory is easy to follow.
critique.problems: Most of each note is initially offscreen, and the long package name creates a conspicuously taller row. The wide notes column makes the table slightly wider than B.
critique.cause: The 489 px Notes column is sized for the widest one-line note; the 220 px Package column wraps the exceptional identifier over three lines.

critique.good: All five fields are visible together, the headers and compact attributes scan clearly, and the advisory wraps at recognizable boundaries.
critique.problems: The long package name occupies three lines, its version splits, and the advisory row is tall. The first note also leaves a short final line.
critique.cause: The 168px package column and 100px version column constrain identifiers; the 229px notes column forces several lines of prose and URL.

critique.good: Package and version are easy to read, notes are reasonably compact, and the mostly two-line rows have a steady rhythm. The status columns remain visible initially.
critique.problems: Most notes lie beyond the initial viewport, so reading context requires scrolling. The advisory wraps within its reference, and the wide package column leaves unused space in most rows.
critique.cause: The 260px package column pushes notes far to the right; 340px for notes is insufficient to keep the complete advisory on one line.

critique.good: Every field is visible at once, the full version stays on one line, and license and vulnerability values are easy to compare.
critique.problems: The advisory breaks inside a word, the moment note takes three lines, and the long package takes three lines. The resulting rows are tall and uneven.
critique.cause: The 217px notes column is too narrow for a clean advisory break and comfortable prose; the 168px package column constrains the long identifier.

critique.good: Most rows are compact, versions and status fields scan well, and notes including the advisory remain on one line in the full table. More of each note appears initially than in d1r1B.
critique.problems: The long package occupies three lines, creating one conspicuously tall row. Much of the notes column is outside the initial viewport, and the one-line notes demand substantial horizontal travel.
critique.cause: The 220px package column creates the tall row, while the 489px notes column produces the largest overall width.

critique.good: All headers and version identifiers stay on one line. The compact status columns are easy to compare, and most of the table is visible initially.
critique.problems: The notes are cramped, the advisory spans several lines, and the long package takes three lines. A small horizontal scroll is still needed to see the end of the notes.
critique.cause: The 168px package and 229px notes columns force wrapping; the 112px version column contributes to a table just beyond the viewport.

critique.good: The notes have a comfortable measure, the status fields remain easy to scan, and the table is less tall than d1r2A.
critique.problems: The long package still takes three lines, and the advisory breaks within its reference. Much of the notes column is outside the initial viewport.
critique.cause: The 220px package column falls short of the width needed for the observed two-line package break, while the 340px notes column and overall width require scrolling.

critique.good: The long package takes two lines, the advisory reference is intact, and the notes read comfortably. The compact attributes remain aligned for comparison.
critique.problems: The wide table leaves most notes off-screen initially and requires substantial horizontal travel to read them.
critique.cause: The 260px package and 420px notes columns improve wrapping but bring the table to 1015px.

critique.good: All fields are visible together without scrolling, and the headers and compact status fields are clear.
critique.problems: The pre-release version breaks across lines, the long package takes three lines, and the advisory note takes four. These breaks slow reading across the affected rows.

critique.good: The long package takes two lines, versions remain whole, and the notes are generally readable with a consistent two-line maximum.
critique.problems: The advisory reference breaks across lines, and most notes require horizontal scrolling. The table is considerably wider than the viewport.
critique.cause: The 340px notes column is too narrow to keep the reference together in its current line context; the 260px package column also pushes notes farther right.

critique.good: All fields are visible together, the compact attributes scan clearly, and the version identifiers stay on one line.
critique.problems: The long package name breaks inside “internal,” making the row identifier harder to recognize. Notes are cramped, and the advisory occupies four lines.

critique.good: The long package name takes two lines at natural breaks, versions and compact attributes remain intact, and no row exceeds two lines.

critique.good: The wider Notes column keeps the advisory URL together and lets the moment note fit on one line. More of Notes is visible initially than in d1r3B.

critique.cause: The first four columns occupy 594px, leaving only about 126px of Notes visible initially; the 420px Notes column is just short of fitting the lodash note on one line.

critique.good: All headers and compact attributes are readable, and more of Notes is visible initially than in the wider scrolling designs. The advisory address remains recognizable.
critique.problems: The long package name occupies three lines, making its row disproportionately tall. Notes still requires scrolling, and the first note wraps for a single trailing word.
critique.cause: Package at 168px creates the three-line identifier; Notes at 420px leaves the first note just short of fitting and extends well beyond the viewport.

critique.good: The full table is compact and easy to scan: notes fit on one line, compact attributes stay whole, and the long package name takes two lines.
critique.problems: At first sight, only the beginning of each note is visible. The large horizontal span makes connecting notes back to packages less convenient.
critique.cause: Package at 260px pushes Notes far to the right, while Notes at 489px makes the table 364px wider than the viewport.

critique.good: All fields are visible together, headers and license values fit, and the long package name wraps at natural breaks.
critique.problems: The long version identifier splits across lines, the advisory address is fragmented, and several tall rows leave large empty areas in the compact columns. Notes are noticeably cramped.

critique.problems: The first note ends with an isolated word, and most of every note is offscreen initially. Compared with d1r4C, the narrower Notes column adds two tall rows while retaining substantial horizontal scrolling.

d2r0B.idea: Use a moderately scrolling, balanced layout that preserves compact audit fields and gives package names and notes comparable space, while allowing the longest identifier and URL to split.

d2r0C.idea: Favor uninterrupted lookup with enough width for every cell on one line, accepting substantial horizontal scrolling to reach Notes.

d3r0A.idea: Fit within 719px, balancing package identification and notes while accepting breaks in the longest package name and advisory URL.

d3r0B.idea: Scroll to preserve every package identifier, version, license and advisory URL intact, with notes prose wrapping naturally.

d3r0C.idea: Give notes their full one-line width for continuous reading, while allowing the long internal package identifier to wrap and using horizontal scrolling.

d1r0A.idea: Fit within 719px, keeping the compact audit fields readable while dividing remaining space between package identification and notes.

d1r0B.idea: Favor package lookup with every package name on one line and enough notes width to keep the advisory URL whole, accepting horizontal scrolling.

d1r0C.idea: Favor continuous reading of complete notes on one line while allowing the longest package name to wrap and using horizontal scrolling.

d1r1B.idea: Scrolling alternative: give the long package name more room than in C while keeping the status fields visible initially, and reduce Notes from its one-line width. This tests a more compact table with readable notes and an intact advisory segment.

d3r2B.idea: Test a more compact scrolling layout: give the long package identifier room to wrap in two lines and keep the advisory's longest unbreakable unit intact, while exposing more of notes at first sight than d3r1B.

d3r2C.idea: Test the minimum practical scrolling width for keeping the full package identifier and the advisory's longest unbreakable unit intact. This retains the identifier lookup advantage of d3r1C with less horizontal travel.

d1r2A.idea: Allow a small horizontal overflow to keep the full version on one line while retaining the cleaner advisory wrapping and compact notes of d1r1A.

d1r2B.idea: Reduce the package width from d1r1B to expose more of the notes initially and reduce scrolling; assess whether the long package's extra line is an acceptable tradeoff.

contrast.idea: Equal widths give excess space to short fields while forcing the package identifier and notes into narrow columns. The long package name and advisory URL would be fragmented, making lookup and continuous reading harder.

d3r2A.why: The version stays on one line and the table fits. The long package wraps at hyphens and the advisory note occupies four lines, making that row relatively tall.

ref_auto.why: The narrow version column splits the prerelease version, and the advisory URL runs past the initial viewport edge. The small scroll distance buys shorter notes but still interrupts lookup.

d1r1A.why: It fits and gives notes slightly more room than B, but the prerelease version breaks across lines. The advisory note still takes four lines.

s1C.why: The full table has even two-line content rows, a shorter package wrap and an intact version. At first sight, however, much of every note lies beyond the viewport, requiring substantial horizontal scrolling.

vc_pref.why: The version remains intact and notes are shorter than in the fitting layouts. The initial viewport cuts off the ends of several notes, but the required scroll is modest.

acceptance.unsure: B is the stronger fitting layout because it preserves the full version; D gives slightly more room to the package and notes. Among scrolling layouts, E has cleaner full-table wrapping, while F keeps more of the notes visible initially; their relative value depends on how often readers need the full notes.
